environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind CloudFront distribution with AWS WAF v2 WebACL. The WebACL includes a custom rate-based rule (threshold: 5 requests per 5-minute window per source IP to /api/v1/upload) combined with a scope-down statement matching Content-Type: multipart/form-data. Additionally, the Fargate task definition specifies a read-only root filesystem with an ephemeral tmpfs mount at /var/app/uploads (size 10MB, noexec). The extracted files directory /var/app/extracted is a separate tmpfs mount (50MB, noexec, nosuid). The task runs as non-root UID 1000 with a Linux capabilities drop of ALL. The CloudFront distribution has a custom origin request policy that strips path traversal sequences (../ and ..\) from the request body via a Lambda@Edge function on origin-request events, though this primarily affects URL paths rather than multipart body content.

config.runtime: ECS Fargate, non-root UID 1000, CAP_DROP ALL
config.filesystem: Read-only root filesystem; /var/app/uploads is tmpfs 10MB noexec; /var/app/extracted is tmpfs 50MB noexec nosuid
config.network: CloudFront -> ALB -> Fargate, WAF WebACL attached to CloudFront
config.rate_limiting: WAF rate-based rule: 5 req/5min per IP on /api/v1/upload with Content-Type scope-down
config.lambda_edge: Origin-request function strips ../ from URL paths (not multipart bodies)
